/-!
# Conjectures around homogeneous topological spaces

This file formalizes the notion of a weakly first countable topological space and some conjectures
around those.

*References:*
* [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology."
  Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46.
  https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

open TopologicalSpace Topology Filter Set
open scoped Cardinal

namespace Homogeneous

/--
A topological space $X$ is called *homogeneous* if for all $x, y \in X$ there is homeomorphism
$f : X \to X$ with $f(x) = y$.
-/
class HomogeneousSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  exists_equiv : ∀ x y : X, ∃ f : X ≃ₜ X, f x = y

/-- Every discrete space is homogeneous. -/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance DiscreteTopology.toHomogeneousSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [DiscreteTopology X] :
    HomogeneousSpace X where
  exists_equiv x y := by
    classical
    use IsHomeomorph.homeomorph (Equiv.swap x y)
      (IsHomeomorph.equiv_of_discreteTopology (Equiv.swap x y))
    rw [IsHomeomorph.homeomorph_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_left]

/-- Problem 13 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every infinite homogeneous compact hausdorff
space contains a non-trivial convergent sequence? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem homogeneousSpace_exists_inj_tendsto :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), ¬ Finite X → T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → ∃ s : ℕ → X, s.Injective ∧ ∃ a : X, Tendsto s atTop (nhds a) := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 14 in [Ar2013]:
Is it possible to represent an arbitrary compact hausdorff space as an image
of a homogeneous compact space under a continuous mapping? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem homogeneousSpace_exists_surjective :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      ∃ (Y : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace Y), T2Space Y ∧ CompactSpace Y ∧ HomogeneousSpace Y ∧
        ∃ f : Y → X, Continuous f ∧ f.Surjective := by
  sorry

/-- A topological space is called ω-monolithic if
the closure of every countable subspace is metrizable. -/
class CountablyMonolithicSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  metrizable_of_closure_of_countable : ∀ ⦃s : Set X⦄, s.Countable → MetrizableSpace (closure s)

/-- Every Metrizable space is ω-monolithic. -/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance MetrizableSpace.countablyMonolithicSpace
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [MetrizableSpace X] : CountablyMonolithicSpace X := by
  refine { metrizable_of_closure_of_countable := ?_ }
  intros
  infer_instance

/-- Problem 15 in [Ar2013]:
Is every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space first countable? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem firstCountableTopology_of_countablyMonolithicSpace :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → FirstCountableTopology X := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 16 in [Ar2013]:
Is the cardinality of every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space not greater than 𝔠? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem countablyMonolithicSpace_card_lt :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → #X ≤ 𝔠 := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 17 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every nonempty ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space contains a point with a
first countable neighborhood basis?

Note: `Nonempty X` is required since the conclusion asserts the existence of a point.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      Nonempty X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → ∃ x : X, (𝓝 x).IsCountablyGenerated := by
  sorry

end Homogeneous

findings.description: Problem 17 assumes monolithicity, but lines 112–113 assume only `CountablyMonolithicSpace X`. That class requires metrizable closures of countable subsets, i.e. ω-monolithicity. For compact Hausdorff spaces, monolithicity requires the corresponding weight bound for closures of subsets of every cardinality, not just countable subsets. The theorem and its docstring therefore pose the stronger ω-monolithic variant instead of the cited monolithic problem. The nonemptiness hypothesis and the conclusion about the neighborhood filter are correct.
findings.source_evidence: Arhangel’skii, Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology (2013), p. 43, Problem 17: “Is it true that every nonempty monolithic compact space is first-countable at some point?” By contrast, Problems 15–16 explicitly say “ω-monolithic.” The cited 1987 reference, Topological homogeneity. Topological groups and their continuous images, §4, p. 106, distinguishes the notions: monolithic means network weight equals density for every subspace; ℵ₀-monolithic means closures of countable subsets have countable network weight. The 2013 PDF was read at https://web.archive.org/web/20260726062340id_/https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf .
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a genuine monolithic predicate and use it, rather than `CountablyMonolithicSpace`, in Problem 17. On compact Hausdorff spaces it can be expressed as `∀ s : Set X, ∃ B : Set (Set (closure s)), IsTopologicalBasis B ∧ #B ≤ max #s ℵ₀`. Update the Problem 17 docstring accordingly, while retaining the existing ω-monolithic hypothesis for Problems 15–16. This candidate predicate and its implication to `CountablyMonolithicSpace` were checked in `/workspace/review/correction.lean`.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for a non-trivial convergent sequence; Lean asks for an injective convergent sequence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In a T1 space, a convergent sequence with finite range is eventually equal to its limit. Thus a non-eventually-constant convergent sequence has infinite range, from which one can extract an injective convergent sequence. Conversely, an injective sequence cannot be eventually constant. If the convention also requires the limit not to occur among the terms, its possible single occurrence can be discarded. The equivalence with the non-eventually-constant formulation was proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, without using any sorry-backed theorem.

sources_consulted: A. V. Arhangel’skii, Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology, Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 2(72)–3(73) (2013), 37–46; read in full at https://web.archive.org/web/20260726062340id_/https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf .

A. V. Arkhangel’skii, Topological homogeneity. Topological groups and their continuous images, Russian Mathematical Surveys 42:2 (1987), 83–131, especially §4, p. 106; DOI 10.1070/RM1987v042n02ABEH001333; read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=rm&paperid=2424&what=fullteng&option_lang=eng .
Russian original of the 1987 reference, §4, pp. 86–90, read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=rm&paperid=2424&what=fullt&option_lang=eng .

Marek Cúth, Characterization of compact monotonically (ω-)monolithic spaces using system of retractions (2014), introduction, preliminaries, and main equivalence; LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1401.7501 .

zbMATH Open bibliographic records and reviews consulted through api.zbmath.org: 6360739 (2013 source), 4046651 (1987 source), 3990324, 943190, 4088470, and 5365227; also the search results for monolithic compact spaces and countable character.

MathOverflow question 419477, What is the name of the (possibly well-known) class of π-monolithic compact spaces?, question body read through the Stack Exchange API: https://mathoverflow.net/questions/419477/ .
review.notes: Checked both classes, both proved instances, and all five problem statements. Problems 13–16 otherwise agree with the source. The paper’s blanket convention that compact spaces are Hausdorff justifies the T2 assumptions, including on the source space in Problem 14. Lean checks covered empty, singleton, and finite spaces, satisfiability using a Cantor cube, and the neighborhood-basis characterization of countable character. The open-status tags agree with the cited survey; no status contradiction was established. All experiments were confined to /workspace/review/.

not_demonstrated.reason: I have no short proof or disproof of the formalized ω-monolithic statement, nor a short Lean construction of a compact Hausdorff space distinguishing the two hypotheses. Finite and metrizable compact spaces satisfy both notions. The existing scratch proof establishes only that monolithicity implies the file’s countable condition; it does not demonstrate a disagreement on a concrete input.

submission.summary: No qualifying trivial demonstration was produced. The optional trivial_proof.lean file is absent.
submission.gave_up_reason: The reported defect replaces an all-cardinal hypothesis with its countable case, without supplying an elementary counterexample or making the statement obviously provable. Demonstrating it concretely would require substantial topology rather than a handful of Lean lines.

submission.summary: Added a monolithic predicate for compact Hausdorff spaces that bounds the basis cardinality of every subset’s closure, and replaced Problem 17’s ω-monolithic hypothesis with it. Updated the docstring and made the existing Hausdorffness and compactness hypotheses instance binders. All other existing declarations remain unchanged. The required compile command succeeds with only the five expected `sorry` warnings; supplementary Lean checks verify finite boundary cases and the implication to ω-monolithicity.
